7-Eleven finally wins permission to build at notoriously busy intersection

by Meta MintonNovember 2, 2026November 2, 2026
💬 ⭐ Prefer on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by

After many years, 7-Eleven has finally won permission to build a gas station at a notoriously busy intersection.

Discover more
Local News Subscription
Villages Event Photos
Online Newspaper Access

The Lady Lake Commission voted 3-2 on Monday night to allow Solid Rock Property Group to construct a 7-Eleven at the corner of Rolling Acres Road and County Road 466.

The commission had previously voted 3-2 to deny the request in May.

In the ensuing months, Solid Rock Property Group negotiated some major concessions, including $350,000 in turn-lane improvements for Rolling Acres Road to be paid for by the developer. Other concessions include a vinyl fence, an enhanced landscape buffer, 24-hour lighting and surveillance cameras.

A fragile majority had stubbornly prevented 7-Eleven from building a convenience store and gas station at the busy location. Commissioners have long been concerned about the impact a 7-Eleven could have on traffic.

Mayor Ed Freeman and Commissioner Treva Roberts voted against the 7-Eleven proposal on Monday night. Commissioners Ed Regan, Amanda McLea and Mike Sage voted for it.

A second reading and final vote are scheduled for Nov. 16.
